subject: Animation
title: Argentine and Chilean Animation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Argentine and Chilean Animation.

hook.text: Argentina produced the world's first animated feature film — El Apóstol by Quirino Cristiani in 1917.

buildup.text: Cristiani used cardboard cutout animation to create a political satire about the Argentine president.

discovery.text: The film predates Disney's Snow White by twenty years, yet it is almost unknown outside animation history circles.

twist.text: All copies of El Apóstol were destroyed in a warehouse fire. The first animated feature is lost forever.

climax.text: Latin America pioneered animation before Hollywood, but the loss of early works erased its place in history.

punchline.text: The world's first animated feature was made in Argentina and lost to fire.

quiz.question: What was El Apóstol's significance in animation history?
options: It was the first animated film shown in color
Made in Argentina in 1917, it was the world's first animated feature film, predating Disney by 20 years
It was the first animated film to use sound

details.summary: Argentine and Chilean animation are growing with distinctive voices. Argentina produced the world's first animated feature film in 1917 and continues innovating, while Chile's student-led animation scene is gaining international festival recognition.
details.whyItMatters: Argentina's claim to the first animated feature predates Disney by two decades. Understanding South American animation history reveals contributions that dominant Hollywood narratives have long overlooked.
takeaways: Argentina produced the world's first animated feature film in 1917
Chilean animation gains recognition through festival circuits
South American animation traditions predate and enrich the global narrative

faq.question: What was the world's first animated feature film?
faq.answer: El Apóstol, a 1917 Argentine political satire by Quirino Cristiani, predates Disney's Snow White by twenty years. Unfortunately, the only copy was destroyed in a fire. Cristiani's lost work reminds us that animation history extends beyond Hollywood.

faq.question: How are Argentine and Chilean animation industries developing?
faq.answer: Both countries have growing animation schools, festival presence, and co-production agreements. Government cultural funding and European partnerships support feature and series production, though sustainable commercial models remain challenging.
